It is main_quantitative_sampling clause 1 (pathLaw F_init F-hat {stopTime = top} = 0). E tau <= (F-hat_term(S) + F_out*(S))/F_init(S) is clause 2, and 's_tau is well defined' is clause 3. The hypotheses are C.1's (F_init != 0, finite measures, no flow matching). added_hypotheses = [] and none was added.

CHECK-1 point 1 is resolved. The sentence 'The stopping decision at time t depends only on s_1, ..., s_t and an independent coin' is gone. l.165 now reads: 'Define the sampling time tau in N_{>=1} u {inf} as the random variable given by P(tau >= 1) = 1 and P(tau = t | tau >= t) = dF_term/d(F_term + F_out*)(s_t), that is, at each t with tau >= t the sampler stops with this probability, by a coin independent of the chain and of the earlier coins, the chain moving on by pi* regardless (a randomized stopping time).'

Compared with Lean's sampler: Y_0 ~ normalize F_init (x) decide, and pathKernel draws y ~ pi(x) from (x, b) in both branches (raiseKernel o pi and decide o pi). A raised flag stays raised; a lowered flag is raised with probability stop(y) by decide. In words: s_1 ~ F_init (pathLaw_spec clause 1); s_{t+1} ~ pi*(s_t) whatever the flag ('the chain moving on by pi* regardless'); and on tau >= t (the flag still lowered before t), the decision at t is a Bernoulli(stop(s_t)) drawn fresh, given the whole past and s_t, with the future chain drawn from s_t afterwards ('a coin independent of the chain and of the earlier coins', in the standard reading U_t iid uniform and independent of the chain, stop iff U_t < h(s_t)). The 'that is' makes this constructive description the definition, so the hazard no longer names a class. Given h, the description fixes the joint law of (chain, tau), with P(tau > t | chain) = prod_{k<=t}(1 - h(s_k)), and for h = stop that law is pathLaw. This is CHECK-1's fix (b) almost verbatim. Theorems 2.1, 3.8 and C.1 and Corollary 3.9 use this one sampler, so they are now about pathLaw.

The look-ahead instance (a decision reading s_{t+1}: 2/3 instead of 1/2) is excluded, since the decision at t uses only s_t and a fresh coin.

CHECK-1 point 3 is resolved. 'tau in N_{>=1} u {inf}' is stopTime : N-infinity = stopIndex + 1, which is top when no flag is raised. P(tau >= 1) = 1 is pathLaw_spec clause 3. 'tau < inf almost surely' (l.188) is sampling_theorem clause 3 and is now a real conclusion. The other uses of tau are consistent with the wider type. E(tau) (l.190) is in [0, inf] (lintegral of stopTime). s_tau (l.168, Theorems 3.8 and C.1) is defined almost surely by those clauses; Lean's sampledState is arbitrary on the null set {tau = inf}. The sums sum_{t=1}^tau (l.413, l.427, l.465, l.466) and the compositions (s_t)_{t=1}^tau and Phi_{k_{tau-1}} o ... o Phi_{k_1} (l.680-681) are read on sampled trajectories, which are almost surely finite under the hypotheses in force. No use needs tau to be finite everywhere.

Theorem 2.1's hypotheses are unchanged and match sampling_theorem: finite F_init and F_term, hterm, and IsFlowMatching. The conclusions match one for one.

The applied text matches the amended corrected. The applied text changes the printed type to N_{>=1} u {inf} and adds the corrected's description to the printed hazard as a gloss, 'that is, ... with this probability', where 'this probability' is the hazard's dF_term/d(F_term + F_out*)(s_t). l.188 adds 'tau < inf almost surely'. The printed P(tau >= 1) = 1 and the hazard are kept, not added. added_hypotheses ('the stopping rule is a randomized stopping time') is the parenthetical at l.165, and no other hypothesis was added. The printed range is now ['main.tex:163-165', 'main.tex:178-185'] and contains both edited v1 lines (164 and 185), so CHECK-1 finding 6 is resolved for C-13. Kind missing-hypothesis, so there is no refutation declaration.

CHECK-1 point 2 is resolved. The footnote now ends: '... is dominated by (F_term + F_out*)/F_init(S), so it charges no (F_term + F_out*)-null set, and the sampler obeys the hazard above for every version.' That is the wording CHECK-1 proposed. 'The law of the sampler does not depend on the version chosen' is gone, from the text and from the marker.

Clause by clause, with G = F_term + F_out*:
(a) F_term << G is fterm_ac_stopBase.
(b) 'Up to a G-null set': rnDeriv is an a.e. class, and the sampler's stop equals it G-a.e. (stop_ae_eq).
(c) The unstopped mass sum_{t>=1} P(tau >= t, s_t in .) is GenerativeFlow.occupation F_term (normalize F_init) (pathLaw_hazard clause 2, the hocc step of pathLaw_spec).
(d) 'Dominated by G/F_init(S)': occupation_le with normalize_add_step gives occupation <= F_init(S)^{-1} G. occupation_ac_of_isFlowMatching gives << G, which is 'charges no G-null set'.
(e) 'The sampler obeys the hazard above for every version': under that domination, pathLaw_hazard_rnDeriv gives P(tau = t, s_t in A) = int_A dF_term/dG d occ_{t-1}, with Mathlib's rnDeriv. Any other version h equals rnDeriv G-a.e., and occ_{t-1} << G, so the integral does not change. That is one setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae step, the same step the proof of pathLaw_hazard_rnDeriv makes from stop.

The claim is now about one sampler (pathLaw) and every version, not about samplers built from different versions. It is the anchor read on the a.e. class that l.157 says the Radon-Nikodym derivative is. The quantified clause is not a declaration of its own (minor finding 5).

The footnote does not mention the sampler of Theorem 3.8 (from F_init to F-hat_term, without flow matching). Its domination is proved by occupation_ac_of_matched. Leaving it out is not an overclaim.
